headline: Mother's phone recovered from suspect in Cumilla teen's murder probe; 3 detained
summary: Police have recovered the phone of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim's mother from a suspect's house, marking a key development in the investigation into the teen's death near Comilla University.
details: Police have recovered the phone belonging to the mother of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, who was found dead near Comilla University. The phone was found at the house of a suspect named Tuhin.
Inspector Mofiz Uddin Bhuiyan of Kotbari Police Outpost confirmed this development. Cumilla Superintendent of Police Anisuzzaman is scheduled to brief the media about the investigation today.
Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar. He was a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School.
Earlier, three young men, Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, were detained in connection with the alleged killing. Police are analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects.

Opratim left home around 3:00 PM on Friday, telling his parents he was going to take photographs with his mother’s iPhone. His body was recovered from the Sananda hillocks on the outskirts of Cumilla on Saturday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after he went missing.

headline_marked: [[Iran sends conditions to US via Qatar]] to end ongoing conflict, awaiting Trump's response
headline: Iran sends conditions to US via Qatar to end ongoing conflict, awaiting Trump's response
summary: Iran has formally submitted conditions to Washington through Qatari mediation to halt the ongoing war. These include a ceasefire, unfreezing assets, and lifting a naval blockade.
details: Iran has formally sent a set of conditions to the United States via Qatari mediation to end the ongoing conflict, a top security official told Al Jazeera. Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, confirmed this in an interview.

Rezaei outlined the conditions: a complete ceasefire on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian assets, and the lifting of the naval blockade. He stressed that accepting these terms is crucial for Washington's own interests, dismissing any threats from President Trump.

The conflict began last month after a joint US-Israeli attack in Iran resulted in the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Qatar and Pakistan have been actively working to bring both nations back to the negotiating table since their previous memorandum of understanding expired.

Rezaei did not rule out the possibility of renewed US attacks, citing strong military assessments, but affirmed Tehran's full preparedness for a final war. He noted that Iran has revised its military strategy, now focusing primarily on the US Navy across the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and Arabian Sea.

Iran recently conducted successful tests of anti-ship missiles equipped with multiple warheads in proximity to US warships, with plans for future enhancements. Rezaei warned that any future Iranian counter-attack would be significantly more intense, targeting US military bases, commercial interests, and companies in the region.

While acknowledging the war is 'still ongoing,' Rezaei emphasized Tehran is pursuing a new strategy to resolve the conflict as quickly as possible. An Al Jazeera correspondent highlighted Rezaei's statements as part of Iran's 'two-pronged message' of maintaining diplomatic channels while preparing for war.

David Des Roches, former Pentagon director for the Arabian Peninsula, suggested Washington might not view these conditions as a serious basis for negotiation, potentially interpreting them as a form of Iranian surrender. However, he noted Iran's significant shift in dropping its previous demand for war reparations.
